identity.real_world_identity_notes: The PMR entry 911 Carrera Cup (964), with 265 hp and five forward gears, is best identified as the inaugural 1990 Porsche 911 Carrera 2 Cup of the 964 generation. Porsche identifies the first Cup car as a 1990 964-based 911 Carrera 2 Cup; Porsche's model-year table distinguishes the 1990–1991 M30/01, G50/03 five-speed car from the later 1992–1993 M64/03, G50/10 cars. The simulator does not expose a chassis number, so this is a model-year/specification identity rather than a unique historical chassis mapping.

The official PMR page lists the 964 Carrera Cup identity, 265 hp, and five-speed manual transmission. Porsche's official history identifies the 1990 debut and 964 generation, while Porsche Club Europe technical data identifies the 1990–1991 Carrera 2 Cup as M30/01 with a Sport clutch and G50/03 five-speed transmission. The 265 hp value separates the early car from the 275 hp 1992–1993 version.

PMR reports a five-speed manual; Porsche Club Europe's exact 1990–1991 Cup row lists G50/03 and five gears; the 1990 specialist history corroborates a five-speed gearbox. The exact 1990 race car is listed as manual, the full-resolution 964 Cup cockpit photograph shows a conventional central manual gear-control area rather than paddles, and the model-year table identifies a five-speed G50/03. The photograph does not make the gate legible, so this establishes a manual H-pattern interface category but not the exact pattern.
